chunks: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Saʿd al-Iskāf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning a slave girl who rode upon another slave girl. Then another slave girl prodded her, so the one being ridden bucked and threw down the rider, and she died. So he ruled that her diyah be divided into two halves between the one who prodded and the one who was prodded.

key_terms.النَّاخِسَةِ: the one who prodded, meaning the person who initiated the harmful act
key_terms.الْمَنْخُوسَةِ: the one who was prodded, whose reaction became part of the causal chain
key_terms.بِدِيَتِهَا: her blood money (diyah), the financial compensation due for the death
key_terms.نِصْفَيْنِ: in two halves, indicating equal apportionment of liability

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام rule on diyah when multiple parties contributed to an accidental death?
ai.summary: This hadith records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in a case of accidental death involving shared causation. He apportioned the diyah equally between the direct instigator and the person whose involuntary reaction contributed to the fatal outcome, showing careful legal assessment of liability.
